blocks.text: Dear Ms. Vasquez:

This letter sets out the terms on which our firm will prepare the site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}, and it will stand as our agreement once you have signed and returned one copy. I have kept it plain, so that it records what we discussed and asks nothing you did not expect from that conversation.
Please read it against what we said to one another. If any term here reads differently from how you understood it, tell me before you sign, and I will put it right.
Scope of the Design

Our firm will prepare the site grading design for the property. The set will include the existing-conditions base, the grading plans, the spot and finished-floor elevations, the cut-and-fill earthwork scheme with quantities, the drainage details required to carry the site to design grade, and the erosion and sediment control notes that accompany a grading submittal. It will be prepared to the standard a municipal public works department expects at review, and the cover sheet will be issued under seal.

We will coordinate the Esparza-Lamb grading set with the roadway, stormwater, and utility sheets, so that the package is internally consistent when it is sealed and issued. Where our design meets work that is properly the site contractor's or another engineer's, our sheets will note the interface and stop there. The scope does not extend to construction-phase services or to material testing, which we would take up separately if you wished.

We will assemble the completed sheets as a submittal package suitable for the public works department's review, and we will respond to the review comments that come back on it as part of this design. Should the review take an unusual turn and require substantial rework, I will raise it with you before that work proceeds.

The design will move in the ordinary phases, from a preliminary grading concept you can react to, through a coordinated set, to the sealed drawings issued for permit and construction. We will hold a short review with you at the preliminary stage, so that the direction is settled before the set is carried to completion.
How We Will Work

I walk a site before I draw it, and I run the earthwork quantities myself rather than accept a figure I have not checked. The design will proceed from the survey you provide and from our own field observations, and I will hold the set to what the ground will actually allow. Nothing leaves this office until it has been reviewed on my desk and I am satisfied it is right.

We will keep you informed as the design develops, in short progress reports and in meetings when a decision needs your input, and we will not let a question that is yours to decide sit unasked. The whole set is reviewed internally before it is issued, and I will not seal a sheet I have not satisfied myself is correct.
The Design Team

The drafting and design production will be carried by Linda Nguyen and Jason Jordan, our design technicians. Linda Nguyen will keep the grading set and the lettered project folder in order, and Jason Jordan will hold the roadway and site sheets and the standard details. I, Mark Todd, will direct the work and will review and seal each sheet before it leaves this office.
Fee and Schedule

Our fee for the design is {{fact:f:E-2001-001.fee}}, a fixed amount for the scope described above. We will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2001-001.start}}, and we expect the design to run about eight months from that date, subject to the timeliness of the survey and of the reviews on your side. If the scope changes in a way that affects the fee, I will raise it with you and we will settle it before the additional work begins.
Fees and Payment

We will invoice against the fee monthly as the work proceeds, and our invoices are due within thirty days of receipt. The fee covers our staff and their time. It does not cover out-of-pocket costs such as reproduction, delivery, agency and permit fees, or outside testing; those we bill at cost, and where they are of any consequence we will agree them with you before they are incurred. A small and routine cost we will simply carry on the next invoice.
Term and Termination

Either of us may end this engagement on fourteen days written notice. If {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} ends it, you will owe us for the work properly performed to that date and for costs already committed on your behalf, and nothing further. On termination we will deliver the work in progress in the form it then stands, and the drawings remain your property to the extent you have paid for them.
Confidentiality

We will treat the information you provide in the course of this work as confidential and use it only for the design. That obligation binds our whole staff and continues after the engagement ends. Drawings we seal and issue become part of the public project record in the ordinary course, and nothing in this paragraph restricts that.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform the design with the care and skill ordinarily exercised by civil engineers practicing in this area at this time, and we stand behind our work to that standard. We do not warrant the performance of contractors or others we do not control, nor the results of construction carried out from our drawings without our involvement. Our liability to you under this engagement is limited to the amount of our fee, except where the law does not permit such a limit.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm practices, and any dispute under it will be heard in the courts of that state. Should any single provision be found unenforceable, the remainder of this letter stands.

If these terms reflect our understanding, please sign both originals below, keep one for your files, and return the other to this office. On receipt I will schedule the site walk, and the work will begin. I look forward to it.
Very truly yours,

The site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} is under way, with our start set for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.start}}. This memo sets the assignments and the first tasks, so the project folder is in order from the beginning and no one waits on a hand-off that was never made.

The aim for the opening weeks is narrow. We open the lettered project folder, set up the sheet index and title blocks, and bring in the survey and the standard details, so that when design begins in earnest the file is already clean. Nothing here is design work yet; it is the groundwork that keeps the design orderly later.

The survey is the first thing we need. I will confirm with the client that we have the current one before we set any grade. Jason Jordan builds the existing-conditions base from it, and the grading plans start on top of that base. Until the base is right, nothing drawn over it can be trusted.

The job itself is straightforward in kind, if not in effort. We are grading a site, routing its drainage, and tying it to the roadway and utilities around it. The value is in getting the file and the coordination right at the start, because a set that is coordinated as it is drawn stays orderly through to issue.
Assignments

items: Linda Nguyen: the grading plans, the project folder, and title-block and revision control across the set.
Jason Jordan: the existing-conditions base, the roadway and site base sheets, the border sheets, and the standard details, each confirmed current before we build on it.
Mark Barrett: logs the executed agreement when it comes back by fax, scans it on the flatbed, and files it in the job folder with the drawings it belongs to.
Debra Vasquez, Vice President of Finance, is our point of contact at the client; approvals and questions on their side route through her.

blocks.text: A note on the file itself. Every sheet is matched to the memorandum that governs it, and revisions are clouded and logged as they are made. That discipline is what lets us pull the current sheet in a hurry when the client calls, so please keep to it from the first print.

Coordination with the client runs through Debra Vasquez. When we need a decision or a document from their side, one of us asks her rather than several of us asking around, so the requests stay in order and nothing is asked twice.
First tasks

items: 1. Open the lettered project folder and file the executed agreement once Mark Barrett has scanned it.
2. Linda Nguyen sets up the sheet index and the title blocks for the grading set.
3. Jason Jordan brings in the base survey, builds the existing-conditions base, and confirms the standard details are the current issue.
4. Confirm the kickoff and site-walk date with Debra Vasquez at {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}.

blocks.text: We will meet briefly each week to keep the set coordinated as it grows. Between meetings, flag anything that does not match, a contour, a callout, or a detail, so it is fixed while it is still small.

Once the folder is open and the survey is mounted, we will start preliminary grading. Bring anything that belongs in the file to me, and I will see it filed in the right place. If a task on this list is unclear, ask before you start it rather than after.

blocks.text: Progress Meeting Minutes
Project: site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}. Subject: design coordination meeting for the Esparza-Lamb set. Prepared by Jason Jordan, Design Technician.
Attendees

items: Linda Nguyen, Design Technician
Jason Jordan, Design Technician
Debra Vasquez, Vice President of Finance, {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}

blocks.text: Discussion

Linda Nguyen reported that the preliminary grading plans have advanced to the point where the finished elevations can be checked against the roadway profile, and it was agreed that the grading set and the roadway sheets should now be reviewed together, so that any conflict between the two is caught while it is still inexpensive to correct.

The drainage details were discussed at some length, and while the general scheme is settled, it was noted that two of the inlet callouts do not yet match the detail they reference, a discrepancy that will be corrected before the set is circulated again. Debra Vasquez asked that the review copy sent to the client be a clean, coordinated set rather than a working print, and that request was accepted without objection.

Jason Jordan raised two observations from the most recent site visit, the first being a low area along the eastern boundary that the current grading routes to the proposed inlet without difficulty, and the second a short run of existing grade near the entrance that will require a supplemental survey shot before the finished elevations there can be fixed. It was agreed that the supplemental shot would be requested, so that the entrance grading is set on measured ground rather than on an interpolation between two distant points.

On the standard details, it was confirmed that the border sheets and the detail library now in use are the current issue, so that no sheet in the set relies on a detail that has since been superseded. It was further observed that the coordination between the grading and roadway sheets is the item most likely to govern the pace of the coming weeks, and it was agreed to keep the two sets under joint review from this point forward.

The group reviewed the schedule against the work remaining and found the design to be progressing in line with the plan, with the coordinated review set identified as the next milestone and the client's comments on that set as the item most likely to determine the pace thereafter. A realistic window for the coordinated set will be confirmed once the inlet callouts and the entrance survey are resolved.
Action Items

rows: Correct the inlet callouts to match the referenced details
Request the supplemental survey shot at the entrance
Coordinate the grading set against the roadway profile
Circulate the coordinated review set to the client
Return the client comments on the coordinated set

blocks.text: The next progress meeting will be set once the coordinated set is ready, and Linda Nguyen will circulate the corrected grading sheets to Debra Vasquez in advance, so that the meeting can be spent on comments rather than on a first reading of the set.
Site Grading Design, Progress Report

The site grading design for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}} is on schedule at the midpoint and remains within the fixed design fee of {{fact:f:E-2001-001.fee}}. The preliminary grading is essentially complete, and the set is now in coordination with the roadway and drainage sheets.

This report covers the current period on the Esparza-Lamb set. It summarizes what was finished, what comes next, and the items that could affect the schedule. It is written for the client, and it is deliberately short.
Status Summary

Design is roughly half complete and tracking to plan. No change to scope or fee is anticipated. The work continues to draw from the survey and from our own field observations, and the set is being kept coordinated as it develops. Contours, elevations, and drainage are checked against one another as they are drawn, so the set does not have to be reconciled all at once near the end. The half that remains is of the same kind as the half now done, so there is no part of the work still ahead that we have not already handled on this set.
Accomplishments This Period

The preliminary grading plans and finished elevations were completed and checked against the roadway profile. Jason Jordan brought the roadway and site base sheets to the same stage, so the two sets can now be reviewed together rather than in isolation. The drainage details were advanced toward final, and the inlet callouts flagged at the last meeting were corrected to match the details they reference.

The earthwork was taken from a first cut-and-fill pass, and the quantities are close enough now to confirm that the site balances without an unusual import or export of material. A supplemental survey shot was taken at the entrance, and the finished grade there now rests on measured ground rather than on an interpolation.

The project folder was brought fully current. Every sheet is tied to the memorandum that governs it, revisions are clouded and logged, and the standard details in use were confirmed to be the current issue. A clean, coordinated review copy of the set is now being assembled for the client.
Upcoming Work

The next period completes the grading set and the earthwork quantities and closes out the drainage details. Jason Jordan will finish the roadway and site sheets in parallel, so the whole package advances together. A coordinated review copy will then go to the client, ahead of the review that precedes sealing and issue.

We will also verify a small number of grades in the field before they are set, so that the finished design rests on the ground as it actually stands and not on the survey alone. Any correction from that verification will be folded into the set before it is circulated for review.

The client review of the coordinated set is the one dependency outside our hands, and the schedule allows for a normal turnaround on it. If the comments come back promptly, the set moves to final and to seal without a pause; a longer review would push the sealed issue by the time it takes, and nothing else. We will send the coordinated copy as soon as it is clean, so the review can begin at the earliest point.
Budget

The work remains within the design fee of {{fact:f:E-2001-001.fee}}. Hours are being logged against the set as it progresses, and the effort spent to date is in line with the portion of the design that is complete. No additional services have been requested, and none are foreseen under the current scope.
Risks and Watch Items

items: Survey gaps: a small area at the north property line may still need a supplemental shot before final grading is set.
Coordination: the grading and roadway sheets must stay aligned as both advance; this is being managed by reviewing them together.
Client review turnaround: the schedule assumes comments on the coordinated set are returned promptly.
Site access and weather: field verification of any grade in question depends on access to the site.

blocks.text: Overall the design is on schedule and on budget, and the next step is to complete the grading set and prepare the coordinated review copy for the client. Prepared by Linda Nguyen, Design Technician.
Progress Meeting Minutes

Attendees

items: Linda Nguyen, Design Technician

Debra Vasquez, Vice President of Finance, {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}

blocks.text: Discussion

Linda Nguyen walked the meeting through the grading set as it now stands, which is nearly complete, with the earthwork scheme, the finished elevations, and the drainage details drawn and coordinated against the roadway and utility sheets. It was agreed that the set has reached the stage at which a full pre-issue check is warranted, and that the remaining work is properly a punch list rather than continued design.

Debra Vasquez presented the client comments on the coordinated review copy, which were limited in number and directed chiefly at the labeling on two of the grading sheets and at a single drainage note, and each comment was reviewed in turn and either accepted for correction or resolved in the meeting. It was confirmed that none of the comments touches the design itself, so that the corrections can be made without disturbing the coordination already achieved between the sets.

The group then reviewed the sheet index against the physical set, sheet by sheet, and confirmed that every sheet listed is present and that no sheet in the set is absent from the index, a check made deliberately at this stage because an index that has drifted from the set is the kind of small error that is easy to miss and awkward to explain after issue. Two sheets were found to carry an old revision letter in the title block, and those will be brought current as part of the punch list.

The meeting closed on the mechanics of issue, and it was confirmed that the title blocks, the border sheets, and the standard details are the current issue, so that the package will be internally consistent when it is submitted for review and seal. It was noted that the cover sheet is to be sealed only after the punch list is cleared and the set has had its final review, and not before.
Action Items

rows: Make the labeling corrections on the two grading sheets
Bring the two title-block revision letters current
Clear the punch list and reconcile the sheet index to the set
Confirm the resolved drainage note back to the client

blocks.text: The clear next step is for Jason Jordan and Linda Nguyen to complete the punch list, after which the coordinated set will be submitted for the firm's final review and seal ahead of issue, and Debra Vasquez will be sent the resolved drainage note for the client file.
